method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill, from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18; a dates module (wrca-dates.l4, built-in date functions only), a seat-neutral core (wrca-core.l4, with 9 regulative definitions for the duties of the worker and the employer: 8 rules and one composition) and two seat layers (wrca-seat.l4 for the injured worker and dependants, wrca-seat-employer.l4 for the employer with its licensed insurer) that restate no rule; no REFUSE (a case the deposit cannot decide returns an explicit not-covered value, asserted); checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Workers Rehabilitation and Compensation Act 1988 (Tas), consolidation published 2025-12-01, current on the site at 2026-10-20, as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/act-1988-004.txt; with the Workers Rehabilitation and Compensation Regulations 2021 (Tas), S.R. 2021 No. 49, consolidation published 2022-02-18, current at 2026-10-20, as deposited at ../../../workers-rehabilitation-and-compensation-regulations-2021/registers/source-bundle/sr-2021-049.txt. The s 71 formula transcriptions were checked against the two source images on 2026-10-24.

checks.l4: stable l4 of VS Code extension legalese.l4-vscode 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset
checks.command: l4 run wrca-dates.l4 ; l4 run wrca-core.l4 ; l4 run wrca-seat.l4 ; l4 run wrca-seat-employer.l4 ; l4 run wrca-cases-core.l4 ; l4 run wrca-cases-worker.l4 ; l4 run wrca-cases-employer.l4
checks.result: 332 assertions written, 332 satisfied (207 core, 66 worker seat, 59 employer seat including 16 mirror cases), 0 errors, 0 warnings (2026-10-24); 9 #TRACEs with an expect line, every one ending in the breach it expects
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read.

scope: In: s 3(1) basic salary (1991 figure only; the current figure is an input), s 65, s 66 (why it is an input); s 25(1) with (1A), (2)(a), (6) as facts; s 32(1)-(3) with s 34(2), ss 37, 38 (inputs); employer duties as regulative rules: s 33A with reg 19 and Sch 1, s 36(1AA), (1)(b), (3)-(5), s 39, s 81(1)-(4), s 81A(1) with s 81AB; s 69(1), (2), (2A), (3), (14); s 70(2), (3); s 69B(1), (2), (2A)-(2D), (2E), (3), (4), (6); s 87(1AA), (1), (4); s 67(1)-(5), s 67A, s 67B(3), (4); s 71(1)-(4), ss 72A(3), (5), 73(1), (4) with reg 20; s 75(1)(b) with reg 21; s 76(1), (3) with reg 22; penalty maxima in ss 33A, 36(3), 39, 81(2) with reg 28 and Sch 2. Out: Part V (dispute procedure, conciliation, medical panels, s 81A(2)-(6), s 81AC), common-law damages and s 138AB, Part XI beyond s 69B(2A), licensing of insurers and self-insurers, ss 25A-28A presumptions, ss 78-80 gradual process, Division 2 medical services beyond the caps, s 86, s 88, ss 82-84B, s 69(4)-(13), s 69B(2DA), (5), s 87(2), (3), ss 67B(1), (2), 67C-67G, s 72 and s 73A beyond inputs, State of connection, deemed workers, asbestos-related disease. Inputs: basic salary for a year (gazetted, s 66), pension age (Social Security Act 1991 (Cth)), the 2022 amendments' commencement read as 1 March 2023 from history notes, State Service Award travel rates (s 76(3), reg 22), the workplace's normal working week and closure days, penalty unit value. Read with subjects/au/social-security-act-1991/encodings/baseline-2026-10/ (pension age; Part 3.14 compensation recovery) and subjects/au/income-tax-assessment-act-1997/ (weekly payments as ordinary income; s 118-37(1)(a) for the lump sum); cross-folder IMPORT is not possible.
seats: the injured worker (and, on a death, the worker's dependants: the spouse or caring partner and dependent children)
the employer, read with its licensed insurer, for the duties the Act puts on them in ss 33A, 36, 39, 81 and 81A
